Gauff's 2026 season started in Australia at the [United Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_Cup "2026 United Cup"), where she helped the defending US team advance to the semifinals to face Poland by defeating [Solana Sierra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solana_Sierra "Solana Sierra") and [Maria Sakkari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maria_Sakkari "Maria Sakkari").[[283]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-283)[[284]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-284) In the semifinals, Gauff defeated Iga Swiatek in straight sets, however, Team United States eventually fell to Poland 2–1.[[285]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-285)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a6/Gauff_-_US_Open_2026_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Gauff_-_US_Open_2026_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Gauff_-_US_Open_2026_\(cropped\).jpg)Coco Gauff practicing at the 2026 US Open
At the [Australian Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Australian_Open_%E2%80%93_Women's_singles "2026 Australian Open – Women's singles"), Gauff advanced to the quarterfinals where she was defeated by Elina Svitolina in straight sets.[[286]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-286)[[287]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-287)
Gauff moved on to the [2026 Qatar Ladies Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Qatar_TotalEnergies_Open_%E2%80%93_Singles "2026 Qatar TotalEnergies Open – Singles"), where she lost her opening round to [Elisabetta Cocciaretto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elisabetta_Cocciaretto "Elisabetta Cocciaretto"), a lucky loser, in straight sets.[[288]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-288) At the [Dubai Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Dubai_Tennis_Championships_%E2%80%93_Women's_singles "2026 Dubai Tennis Championships – Women's singles"), Gauff, as the third seed, defeated [Anna Kalinskaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anna_Kalinskaya "Anna Kalinskaya"), Elise Mertens, and [Alexandra Eala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexandra_Eala "Alexandra Eala") on her way to the semifinals, before falling to Svitolina in three sets in just over three hours.[[289]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-289)
As the fourth seed at [Indian Wells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_BNP_Paribas_Open_%E2%80%93_Women's_singles "2026 BNP Paribas Open – Women's singles"), Gauff faced Eala again in the third round and was eliminated retiring due to an arm injury.[[290]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-290) However, she would go on to play in [Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Miami_Open_%E2%80%93_Women's_singles "2026 Miami Open – Women's singles"), where she won her second round rematch against Cocciaretto in three sets.[[291]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-291) Gauff then defeated compatriot [Alycia Parks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alycia_Parks "Alycia Parks") in three sets to advance to the fourth round.[[292]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-292) Despite dropping the second set, Gauff would defeat [Sorana Cîrstea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sorana_C%C3%AErstea "Sorana Cîrstea") in three sets to reach the quarterfinals for the first time in her career.[[293]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-293) Next, she defeated 12th seed [Belinda Bencic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Bencic "Belinda Bencic").[[294]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-294) In the semifinals, she defeated [Karolina Muchová](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karolina_Muchov%C3%A1 "Karolina Muchová") to reach her first final at her home WTA 1000 event.[[295]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-295) Despite battling back to take the second set, Coco Gauff would eventually lose the final against Aryna Sabalenka in three sets.[[296]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-296)[[297]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-:4-297)
At the [Italian Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Italian_Open "2026 Italian Open"), Gauff defeated [Tereza Valentova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tereza_Valentova "Tereza Valentova") in straight sets in the second round.[[298]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-298) She then went on to earn comeback wins in her next three matches from a set down, defeating Solana Sierra, [Iva Jovic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iva_Jovic "Iva Jovic") and [Mirra Andreeva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mirra_Andreeva "Mirra Andreeva") to reach the semifinals.[[299]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-299)[[300]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-300)[[301]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-301) Gauff then advanced to the final for the second consecutive year, after defeating Sorana Cîrstea in straight sets.[[302]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-302) In the final, Gauff met Svitolina for the third time in 2026. Despite coming back to take the second set in a tiebreak, Gauff eventually lost the final in three sets.[[303]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-303) At the French Open, as the defending champion, she was upset by 28th seed [Anastasia Potapova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anastasia_Potapova "Anastasia Potapova") in the third round, after winning the first set, marking the first time she failed to reach at least the quarterfinals since 2020.[[304]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-304) As a result, Gauff fell from the top 5 in the singles rankings after 137 consecutive weeks.
Gauff came into [Wimbledon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Wimbledon_Championships_%E2%80%93_Women's_singles "2026 Wimbledon Championships – Women's singles") without a grass-court win in two years.[[305]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-korpatsch-305) However, she beat [Tamara Korpatsch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamara_Korpatsch "Tamara Korpatsch") in the first round.[[305]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-korpatsch-305) She reached the fourth round following three-set wins over Solana Sierra[[306]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-306) and qualifier Claire Liu.[[307]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-307) She came from a set down to beat No. 11 Belinda Bencic and reach the quarterfinals at Wimbledon for the first time.[[308]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-308) She came from a set down to defeat No. 4 Jessica Pegula and reach her first Wimbledon semifinal.[[309]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-wimbledon-309) She has now reached the semifinals at all four Grand Slam events.[[309]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-wimbledon-309) She lost in the semifinals to No. 9 Karolína Muchová, despite holding a match point in the third-set tiebreak.[[310]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-310)[[311]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-311)
Gauff then entered [Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_National_Bank_Open_%E2%80%93_Women's_singles "2026 National Bank Open – Women's singles") as the fourth seed where fell in three sets to Elena Rybakina in the semifinal.[[312]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-312) It was their second match in four years.[[313]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-313) Gauff then won her fourth WTA 1000 title in [Cincinnati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Cincinnati_Open_%E2%80%93_Women's_singles "2026 Cincinnati Open – Women's singles"), defeating compatriot Jessica Pegula in straight sets.[[314]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-314)
Gauff advanced to the semifinal of [2026 US Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_US_Open_%E2%80%93_Women's_singles "2026 US Open – Women's singles") before being eliminated by [Elena Rybakina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elena_Rybakina "Elena Rybakina").[[315]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-315)
In October, Gauff played in the [China Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_Open_\(tennis\) "China Open \(tennis\)") and fell in the Round of 16 to [Elise Mertens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elise_Mertens "Elise Mertens") in straight sets. She subsequently qualified for her 5th straight [WTA Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WTA_Finals "WTA Finals").[[316]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-316)
## Rivalries
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Coco_Gauff&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Rivalries")]
### Iga Świątek
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Coco_Gauff&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Iga Świątek")]
Gauff and [Iga Świątek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iga_%C5%9Awi%C4%85tek "Iga Świątek") have met 16 times since 2021, with Świątek controlling the head-to-head 11–5.[[317]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-317) Gauff lost to Świątek in her first [major](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Slam_\(tennis\) "Grand Slam \(tennis\)") final at the [2022 French Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_French_Open_%E2%80%93_Women's_singles "2022 French Open – Women's singles") championships.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-:1-128) They met again in the [2023 French Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_French_Open_%E2%80%93_Women's_singles "2023 French Open – Women's singles") quarterfinal, and the [2024 French Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_French_Open_%E2%80%93_Women's_singles "2024 French Open – Women's singles") semifinal, with Świątek winning each time.[[318]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-318)[[319]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-319) Gauff has won their last four meetings, including the [2024 WTA Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_WTA_Finals_%E2%80%93_Singles "2024 WTA Finals – Singles") and most recently at the [2026 United Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_Cup "2026 United Cup").[[240]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-:3-240)[[320]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-320)[[321]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-321)
### Aryna Sabalenka
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Coco_Gauff&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Aryna Sabalenka")]
Gauff and [Aryna Sabalenka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aryna_Sabalenka "Aryna Sabalenka") have developed a noteworthy rivalry, competing in multiple major finals. Their contrasting demeanors and styles of play shine throughout in their matches. The two have met 13 times since 2020, with Sabalenka having the edge in their head-to-head at 7–6.[[322]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-322) Gauff won her first major title by defeating Sabalenka in the [2023 US Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_US_Open_%E2%80%93_Women's_singles "2023 US Open – Women's singles") final.[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-:2-195) Sabalenka would then defeat Gauff on her way to defending her title in the [2024 Australian Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Australian_Open_%E2%80%93_Women's_singles "2024 Australian Open – Women's singles") semifinal.[[323]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-323) Gauff defeated Sabalenka in the [2024 WTA Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_WTA_Finals_%E2%80%93_Singles "2024 WTA Finals – Singles") semifinal on her way to winning the tournament.[[240]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-:3-240) Gauff would then win her second [major](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Slam_\(tennis\) "Grand Slam \(tennis\)") title at the [2025 French Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_French_Open_%E2%80%93_Women's_singles "2025 French Open – Women's singles") by defeating Sabalenka in three sets.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-:0-4) After a close first set, Sabalenka avenged her French Open loss by knocking Gauff out of the [2025 WTA Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_WTA_Finals_%E2%80%93_Singles "2025 WTA Finals – Singles") where Gauff was the defending champion in straight sets.[[324]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-324) Gauff and Sabalenka would face off in the [2026 Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Miami_Open_%E2%80%93_Women's_singles "2026 Miami Open – Women's singles") final, where Sabalenka defeated Gauff in three sets.[[297]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-:4-297)
## Playing style and coaching
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Coco_Gauff&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Playing style and coaching")]
While hard court is Gauff's favorite surface, she has yielded her best results on clay. Although many analysts would describe her as an "opportunistic counterpuncher",[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] she describes herself as having a highly aggressive playing style and a powerful serve, while on the defensive side she uses her athleticism and speed to remain in points.[[325]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-325)
From July 2023 to September 2024 her coach was [Brad Gilbert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Gilbert "Brad Gilbert").[[326]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-326) Gilbert encouraged Gauff to put high, heavy topspin on her ball and to chase down balls in every corner of the court.[[327]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-auto3-327) In September 2024 Gauff hired coach Matt Daly,[[328]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-328) who has focused on improving her serve and forehand with a grip on her racket that is closer to the [eastern backhand style](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grip_\(tennis\) "Grip \(tennis\)") rather than the more frequently used [continental style](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grip_\(tennis\) "Grip \(tennis\)").[[327]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-auto3-327) In August 2025, Gauff replaced Daly with Gavin MacMillan, a biomechanics specialist who helped rescue Aryna Sabalenka's serve.[[329]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-329)[[330]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-330)[[331]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-331)

## Other ventures
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Coco_Gauff&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Other ventures")]
In June 2020, Gauff gave a speech at a [Black Lives Matter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Lives_Matter "Black Lives Matter") protest in her hometown of Delray Beach, Florida, following the [murder of George Floyd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder_of_George_Floyd "Murder of George Floyd").[[356]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-356)
In January 2025, Gauff became an investor in [Unrivaled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unrivaled_\(basketball\) "Unrivaled \(basketball\)"), a professional women’s basketball league, to help elevate women’s sports.[[357]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-357)[[358]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-358)
In April 2025, Gauff left her longtime agency Team8 and launched her own management firm, Coco Gauff Enterprises, in partnership with [WME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WME_Group "WME Group").[[359]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-359) In September 2025, Gauff's media company, IROC, partnered with Religion of Sports for production and branded content.[[360]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-360) In August 2026, Tennis Channel released two short documentaries: _Serve: Fashion & Tennis_ and _The Zina Effect_ , executive produced by Gauff.[[361]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-361)[[362]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-362) Gauff featured in the music video for American rapper [Gunna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunna_\(rapper\) "Gunna \(rapper\)")'s October 2026 single "Pop It".[[363]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-363)
## Personal life
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Coco_Gauff&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Personal life")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c5/Coco_Gauff_at_2022_Boston_Celtics_game-1.jpg/250px-Coco_Gauff_at_2022_Boston_Celtics_game-1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Coco_Gauff_at_2022_Boston_Celtics_game-1.jpg)Gauff in 2022
Gauff is a [Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity "Christianity"). Since she was eight years old, she has prayed with her father before every match that she and her opponent would be safe. After winning the Cincinnati Open in August 2023, she said: "... I'd like to thank my Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ. I spent a lot of nights alone, crying trying to figure it out. I still have a lot to figure out, but I thank Him for covering me." After winning her first major title in September 2023, she said: "... I don't pray for results, I just ask that I get the strength to give it my all and whatever happens happens. I'm so blessed in this life."[[364]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-364)
Gauff's tennis idols are Serena and Venus Williams. "Serena Williams has always been my idol...and Venus," she has said. "They are the reason why I wanted to pick up a tennis racquet."[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-upi-17) Gauff first met Serena when she won the Little Mo' national tournament at the age of eight, and later met her again to film a commercial for [Delta Air Lines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delta_Air_Lines "Delta Air Lines") and at the Mouratoglou Academy.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-gauff-hopes-14) After defeating Venus Williams at Wimbledon in 2019, Gauff expressed her respect when they shook hands at the net. "I was just telling her thank you for everything she's done for the sport," Gauff said. "She's been an inspiration for many people. I was just really telling her thank you."[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-nyt-venus-39)
Gauff stated in 2020 that she had experienced [depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depression_\(mood\) "Depression \(mood\)") and stress related to her sporting career, though her parents clarified that she was not diagnosed with depression in the clinical sense, and had not sought medical attention relating to her psychological well-being.[[365]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-365)
Gauff is a fan of [anime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anime "Anime"), including _[My Hero Academia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_Hero_Academia "My Hero Academia")_.[[366]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-366) She runs an "editing account" on TikTok, mainly of anime dramas.[[367]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-367)
Gauff is a fan of popular YouTubers and streamers [Ludwig Ahgren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludwig_Ahgren "Ludwig Ahgren"), [Valkyrae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valkyrae "Valkyrae"), and [Kai Cenat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kai_Cenat "Kai Cenat").[[368]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-368)
In July 2023, Gauff and actress [Storm Reid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storm_Reid "Storm Reid") helped fund a new playground and purple-painted tennis courts in East Atlanta's [Brownwood Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brownwood_Park "Brownwood Park").[[369]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_Gauff#cite_note-369)
